statement: A round pizza has radius $8$ inches. The crust is a ring $3$ inches wide all the way around the outside edge, and the rest of the pizza is a circle of toppings with the same center. What is the area of the crust, in square inches?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the two circumferences, $16\pi - 10\pi = 6\pi$, but that is a difference of lengths, not an area.
I subtracted the radii first and then squared, $\pi(8 - 5)^2 = 9\pi$, which is the area of a small circle of radius 3, not of the ring.
I unrolled the crust into a strip as long as its inner edge, $10\pi$, and 3 wide, but the outer edge of the crust is longer than the inner edge.
I unrolled the crust into a strip as long as its outer edge, $16\pi$, and 3 wide, but the inner edge of the crust is shorter than that.

hints: The crust is the whole pizza with the circle of toppings cut out of it.
The circle of toppings has radius $8 - 3 = 5$. Subtract its area from the area of the whole pizza.

solutions.reliable: The circle of toppings has radius $8 - 3 = 5$ inches. The crust is the whole pizza with that circle removed, so its area is $\pi \cdot 8^2 - \pi \cdot 5^2 = 64\pi - 25\pi = 39\pi$ square inches.
solutions.elegant: Straighten the ring into a strip $3$ inches wide whose length is the circle through the middle of the crust, radius $6.5$: $2\pi(6.5) \cdot 3 = 39\pi$. The middle circle balances the shorter inner edge and the longer outer edge, which is why $30\pi$ and $48\pi$ miss on either side.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
